Sam: Quick heads-up — noticed repeated KV rehydration during mixed short->long flows. Latency tails spike ~60-120ms after commit 3f4b2e. Logs below.
```log
[evict] slab=27 page=981 tenant=acme prefix=f_hX3 rehydrate_ms=24
[rehydrate] keys=3 bytes=12KB slot_pulses=2
[kernel-switch] new_kernel=quant-avx512 cost_ms=2.4
```
Maya: Which axis — eviction policy or key design? Can you paste eviction counters?
Sam: Counters: 
```json
{"evict_count":1274, "rehydrations":392, "cross_request_reuse":0.18}
```
perf-bot: profile summary (last 1h): KV rehydrate hotpath accounts for 38% of token latency; batch-coalescer drop-in after kernel change increased prefix misses by 12%; heavy longctx sessions push memory growth due to fragmented page allocations. Link: https://perf.internal/runs/1758889999
Chris: Sounds like fragmentation + key churn. Proposal: move to 64-bit compact key: hash(tenant|prefix) ^ (session_id>>8) and keep a small per-session sticky bucket to avoid cross-slab relocations. This reduces key entropy across slabs.
Maya: Also try hinting routing: if request.longctx then route to same slab via sticky_hint header; reduces cross-request page handoffs and rehydrations.
Sam: Repro steps attached: small script that simulates N=200 short prefixed requests then a single longctx -> see rehydrate spike.
```bash
for i in {1..200}; do curl -H "X-Prefix: abc" https://canary.generate.internal/v1; done
curl -H "X-LongCtx: 1" https://canary.generate.internal/v1
```
Chris: One more datapoint — kernel selector introduced prefetch-avoid flag in 3f4b2e to reduce prefetch during small batches; that may have increased evictions for shared slabs. Rolling it back in canary should show improvement.
Maya: Agreed. Plan: 1) canary rollback kernel flag on one pool 2) enable sticky_hint for longctx routes 3) instrument per-slab fragmentation metric (free_pages, avg_run_length). Run 24h canary and compare rehabs/evict ratio.
Sam: I'll open a tiny playbook and put quick checks into console dashboard. cc @perf-bot for telemetry alerts. :thumbsup:
